Prices help

Prepare a daily price file

This guide opened in a new tab. Close this tab to return to Prices. Your imported prices stay in the app tab.

You can load daily prices from a JSON file (a plain-text format for structured data) and see them on the Prices page. Imported data is chart context only. It cannot create a paper trade (a practice trade with no real money) or give the journal prices.

A successful import immediately replaces the current imported batch. It stays in that tab until you reload. A rejected file keeps the previous data. Keep your original file.

Steps

  1. Copy the synthetic example (invented data for practicing the format) from the next section, or start from your own data.
  2. Fill in the fields described below. Use null for unknown values where this page allows it.
  3. Save the file as UTF-8 text (the standard encoding most text editors use) with a .json extension.
  4. In Cribscore, open Prices → Import daily price data. Choose the file, then select Import price data.
  5. Read the message under the company picker on the Prices page. If the file was rejected, look up its words under “If the import is rejected”.

The example uses invented data

Every value, symbol and timestamp in this example is invented. It is only for practicing the format. It is not real market data, past or present. It has no verified source, trading calendar, record of splits and dividends, or chart link.

The complete JSON is below. Copy it into a UTF-8 text file with a .json extension to practice the format. It imports with warnings on purpose. Reading this page does not import anything. Keep the app open in its original tab.

Fields to prepare

One series (the daily prices for one company)
FormatschemaVersion: "cribscore-price-series-v1", a distinct id, an uppercase symbol and a three-letter currency such as USD.
Trading daysinterval: "1d" and a sessionTimezone given as an IANA time zone (a standard place name such as America/New_York). Write each session (the trading day the prices belong to) as the exchange’s local date, YYYY-MM-DD.
PricesWrite open, high, low and close as quoted decimal text, such as "10.25". Keep every digit the source gave. Do not convert them to floating-point numbers first (computer numbers that can change the last digits). The high must be at or above the open and close. The low must be at or below them.
VolumeA number, or null when volume is unknown. Unknown volume is not zero. Ordinary share volume must be a whole number. Split-adjusted volume (rescaled so older values match after a stock split) may have a fraction. Set volumeBasis to shares, split_adjusted_shares or unknown.
Sourcesource.provider (the company that supplied the data) and source.dataset (the name of the data product) must not be empty. Set channel: "manual_import". Use null for an unknown url, capturedAt, publishedAt, responseSha256 or declaredDelayMinutes (how many minutes late the source says its data is). A known URL must use HTTPS and contain no credentials. A known responseSha256 (a fingerprint of the exact file the source sent) is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (digits 0–9 and letters a–f). Do not invent a capture time or digest to clear a warning.
AdjustmentsSet priceBasis to unadjusted, split_adjusted, total_return_adjusted (also adjusted as if dividends were reinvested) or unknown. Use the basis your source establishes. Have you confirmed every corporate action (an event like a split or dividend that changes shares) for these dates? If not, use actions.status: "unknown" with items: []. An empty list does not certify that no actions occurred.

Three fields are optional: originalSymbol, entityId and exchange. They keep the source’s identity for the company when you know it. Leave them out or set them to null when you do not.

You do not need to write the decimals fields. The app creates them. If you re-import a normalized file (one that already has decimals fields), keep its numbers and decimal text consistent.

The data table and the large closing price keep your exact digits. Trailing zeros that do not change the value may disappear, so 10.50 shows as 10.5. The plot is approximate. So are the values under “Benchmark comparison”, where both series start at 100 on their first shared day.

Keep the clocks separate

capturedAt is the time the data was actually retrieved from the source. publishedAt is a publication time you know separately. Write both as exact UTC timestamps (Coordinated Universal Time, ending in Z) with seconds, such as 2020-01-08T22:00:00Z. You may add 1–3 fractional digits. Publication must not come after capture. Where a field allows null, keep unknown values null. When you import the same data later, keep its original clocks.

If a bar (one trading day’s prices and volume) has an availableAt (when those prices became available), it must be a valid UTC timestamp. It must be no earlier than known publication and no later than known capture. Take care here, because an invalid value rejects the file. If it is omitted or null, the parser uses capture, then known publication, or leaves availability unknown. A session date alone is not the time a price was quoted.

Limits

  • The form accepts JSON files only.
  • At most 2 MiB per file (2,097,152 bytes, about 2.1 MB).
  • At most 16 series per file, 5,000 bars (one bar per trading day) per series and 40,000 bars in total.
  • Each session date must be unique within its series. IDs and symbols must be unique within a batch.
  • Duplicate JSON keys are rejected.
  • Prices must be positive. They can have up to 12 decimal places, with a maximum value of 1000000000000 (one trillion).
  • Decimal text cannot contain commas, currency signs or exponents (such as 1e6).

Several companies in one file

To keep several companies together, put their complete series objects in the series list of a wrapper: {"schemaVersion": "cribscore-price-import-v1", "series": []}. The list holds 1–16 series. Each successful upload replaces the previous batch, so put every company you want to see in the same file.

What imported data does not prove

Imports do not provide a verified exchange calendar (the official list of trading days). A continuous line does not prove that holidays, early closes or missing trading days are covered. A recent capture does not mean prices are current. An unknown delay is not zero. An empty action list does not prove that no splits or dividends occurred.

A successful import does not verify your source rights or account entitlement (what your data plan allows). It does not create a paper trade, supply journal marks (prices the journal uses to value decisions) or change rankings. TradingView (a separate charting site that the app can show) never shows your file.

Raw provider responses need conversion to this format, with their original source metadata. This includes Alpaca bars (Alpaca is a company that provides stock market data). Importing them does not connect or authenticate a provider account. Never put account keys or passwords in the file or in a source URL. To connect a price source, open Price-feed setup at the bottom of the Prices page. Its link “How to set up the price feed” opens the setup guide.

If the import is rejected

Your previous data stays in place. The message under the company picker lists each problem in words, such as “bar price invalid”. Open the list below and find those words.

Show every message and its fix

The whole file

“Choose a JSON price file under 2 MiB.”
No file was chosen, or the file is larger than 2 MiB.
import size invalid
The text is larger than 2 MiB.
import parse failed
The text is not valid JSON. Look for a missing comma, quote or bracket, or extra text after the end.
import duplicate key
A field name appears twice in the same object.
import nesting too deep
Lists and objects are nested more than 64 levels deep.
import series count invalid
The file has no series, or more than 16.
import bar count invalid
The file has more than 40,000 bars in total.
import duplicate series
Two series share an id or a symbol.
import validation failed
At least one series broke a rule. The words after it name the rule.

Series fields

price series invalid, price series missing
An entry in the series list is empty or is not a JSON object.
schema version unsupported
Each series needs "cribscore-price-series-v1". A wrapper needs "cribscore-price-import-v1". With a wrong wrapper version the app reads the whole file as one series, so many messages appear at once.
security identity invalid
Check id, symbol and currency. A symbol uses capital letters, digits and a few marks such as a dot or dash, up to 20 characters. A currency is three capital letters.
security mapping invalid
originalSymbol is not written like a symbol, or entityId is empty.
exchange invalid
exchange is empty. Give a name or use null.
session timezone invalid
Use an IANA time zone such as America/New_York.
daily interval required
interval must be "1d".
price basis invalid, volume basis invalid
Use one of the values listed in the table above.

Source fields

source identity required
The source object is missing, or its provider or dataset is empty or longer than 500 characters.
source url invalid
Use an HTTPS address without a user name, password or # part. Its query cannot carry a key, token or password. Or use null.
source capturedAt invalid, source publishedAt invalid
Write exact UTC with seconds, such as 2020-01-08T22:00:00Z.
publication after capture
publishedAt is later than capturedAt.
source digest invalid
responseSha256 must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or null.
source delay invalid
declaredDelayMinutes must be zero or more, or null.
source price session invalid
priceSession must be "regular_daily_aggregate", "unknown" or null.
source pagination status invalid
paginationComplete must be true, false or null.

Bars

bars shape invalid
bars is missing, is not a list, or has more than 5,000 entries.
bar session invalid or duplicate
A session is not a real YYYY-MM-DD date, or the date repeats.
bar price invalid
A price is zero or less, has more than 12 decimal places, is above 1000000000000, or contains a comma, sign or exponent.
bar ohlc inconsistent
A high is below the open or close, or a low is above them.
bar volume invalid
A volume is negative, too large or not a number. A fraction is allowed only when volumeBasis is split_adjusted_shares.
bar decimal projection invalid
In a re-imported file, a decimals entry does not match its number.
bar availability invalid
availableAt is not exact UTC, or it is earlier than known publication or later than known capture.

Splits and dividends

actions shape invalid, action coverage invalid, action identity invalid, split ratio invalid, dividend invalid, action source invalid
Something in actions does not follow the format. If you have not checked splits and dividends, use "status": "unknown" with "items": [].
